admission.justification: No single shaping or log rule bounds the caller experience alone: the choke's strip-and-cap needs the short-form ceiling for over-bound answers, the ceiling needs log placement and byte budgets for the record, and the per-tool table needs all three to state each answer's contract; together they make every answer bounded and every admitted call recorded, while unadmitted writes are dropped and counted by the log's admission rules.

guarantee: Every tool answer holds only what its caller needs next within its bound, and every admitted call leaves its whole record in the daily log under the byte budgets: the choke strips the envelope and caps lists, over-bound answers leave as measured short forms, the log files lines and details with secrets omitted, terminating calls route to the root, and the per-tool table states each answer's fields, uses, cases and bounds — writes that cannot be admitted (folder-budget conflict, oversize detail, unwritable location) are dropped and counted, never failing the call — so a later leaf rebuilding any answer inherits the same ceiling, placement and contract.
title: One bounded answer with its record
